audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and Level 6 read Skill on both layers while the prose says 'you maintain your edge' and 'your lead becomes decisive'; 2+ items read Riven while whys[6], spikes[3] and late all give it to Yasuo. Packet chart: Riven, Riven, Yasuo.
audit.why: 53.83% over 3043 games — a lane Riven wins early and loses to Infinity Edge; the chart understated the early lead and inverted the late one.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 -> Riven, Level 6 -> Riven, 2+ items -> Yasuo, as three matched full/content pairs plus the 2+ items rating.

audit.why: Four spikes present and ordered: Lvl 2-3 W stun, Lvl 6 Blade of the Exile, 1st item, 2+ items Infinity Edge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places (whys[4], spikes[1], mid) claim Last Breath 'requires a knockup source he can't produce alone in a solo lane'. Steel Tempest at 2 stacks of Gathering Storm fires a whirlwind that knocks Airborne — Yasuo generates his own R setup with no jungler at all. The same passages call Wind Slash an execute, and Wind Wall is written as one word.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup stated backwards: a player told his ult is conditional will stand in the Q3 line and get knocked up into a free Last Breath.
audit.corrected: Steel Tempest (4s) knocks up on the 2-stack cast and self-enables Last Breath (70/50/30s). Wind Slash is one ranged projectile per R, and Wind Wall (25/23/21/19/17s, 4s duration) blocks it outright.

audit.why: Wind Wall is correctly named as the cooldown to track before committing R in late and wants.you[1]; its 17-25s window is now stated.
The Wind Wall blocking Riven's R projectile is already stated in mid and late — the interaction the calibration notes flag as commonly missed is present here.

edits.before: Your Level 6 spike is unconditional — Blade of the Exile adds range and Wind Slash execute — while his Last Breath needs a knockup source he can't produce alone in the top lane.
edits.after: Your Level 6 spike is real — Blade of the Exile adds range and one ranged Wind Slash — but Last Breath (70s) needs a knockup and his own 2-stack Steel Tempest supplies it solo.

edits.before: Your R extends range and adds the Wind Slash execute; his R still requires a knockup source he doesn't have in a solo lane, so your spike is unconditional while his isn't.
edits.after: Your R extends range and adds one ranged Wind Slash; his R needs a knockup, but the 2-stack Steel Tempest tornado provides it — never stand in a line once he has two stacks.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you maintain your edge as long as you don't let him poke you with back-to-back Q autos from the edge of his range — stay off the wall side so his Q3 tornado has no corner to trap you. At Level 6 your lead becomes decisive: Blade of the Exile gives you ranged AoE on your third Q cast and a massive execute in Wind Slash, while his Last Breath still requires a knockup he can't self-generate in a solo lane without jungle assistance. The play is to E in, W-stun him, Q-Q-Q through him, then fire Wind Slash at low HP — but watch where his Windwall lands. Yasuo will throw Windwall reactively the instant he sees your R animation; the answer is to position so the Windwall doesn't cover your angle, or simply delay Wind Slash by half a second until he's moved past his own wall. Don't burn your E shield on his Q pokes; save it for the all-in so it absorbs a portion of his crit burst.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you keep the edge as long as you don't eat back-to-back Steel Tempest pokes from the edge of his 475 range — and never stand in a line once he holds two Gathering Storm stacks, because that cast fires the tornado that knocks you up. He self-generates the Last Breath setup; no jungler required. At Level 6 your lead is still real: Blade of the Exile adds range and one ranged Wind Slash, and Last Breath is a 70-second cooldown at rank 1. The play is E in, W-stun him, Q-Q-Q through him, then fire Wind Slash — but watch his Wind Wall. He throws it reactively the instant he sees your R animation and it deletes the projectile outright, so re-angle, or delay half a second until he has moved past his own wall. Don't burn your E shield on Steel Tempest chip; save it for the all-in so it eats part of his crit burst.

edits.before: Angle Wind Slash around his Windwall or bait W before committing to R-execute
edits.after: Angle Wind Slash around Wind Wall (17-25s) or bait it out before you commit your R

edits.before: Keep Windwall between your Wind Slash and himself to nullify your R execute
edits.after: Keep Wind Wall between himself and your Wind Slash — it deletes the projectile

notes: Packet suspectNames flagged 'Steel Tempest Qs' in early as a probable wrong name — it is correct, a false positive; no change made there. The genuine defect was the repeated claim that Yasuo cannot set up his own ultimate. Full-layer prose carries mojibake em dashes on disk, so full-layer edits are limited to clean-ASCII enum fields.
